title: Networks & Topologies: Foundations
welcome_lead: How do computers talk? Let's connect the dots.
meta_desc: GCSE Computer Science adventure on networks, LAN/WAN and network topologies.
final_note: You can describe how networks are built and what topology they use.

concepts.def: Two or more devices connected to share data.
Local area network — small area, e.g. a school.
Wide area network — large area, e.g. the internet.
The shape of a network's connections.
All devices connect to a central switch.
Every device connects to many others directly.

walkthroughs.body_html: A LAN spans a single site — your school's computers and printer. A WAN links LANs across cities or countries. The internet is the world's biggest WAN.
All devices link to a central switch. If one cable fails, only that device drops. Easy to add new devices. Downside: the switch is a single point of failure.
Multiple paths between devices, so messages reroute around failures. Very robust but uses lots of cabling. Common in wireless mesh networks for big homes.
